title: Blichfeldt's Theorem: k+1 Congruent Points When vol > k

problemStatement.formal: \text{If } S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \text{ is measurable with } \mathrm{vol}(S) > k, \text{ then } S \text{ contains } k+1 \text{ points with pairwise differences in } \mathbb{Z}^n
problemStatement.plain: Blichfeldt's theorem (1914): any measurable set S in R^n with volume > k contains k+1 distinct points x_1,...,x_{k+1} whose pairwise differences all lie in the integer lattice Z^n. Unlike Minkowski's theorem, no convexity or symmetry is needed.
